rationale: Round 4 plan: the round 2 overrides already met print_requirements.json; the plate changed in rounds 3 and 4 (6 mm plate, MARGIN 8, Ø10 columns, reversed coxa windows), so it is sliced again. Stock 0.20mm QUALITY @MK3 + Prusament PETG (filament_type PETG = print_requirements; 250 °C, first layer 240, bed 90/85, fan 30-50 %: inside 230-250 / 80-90 and the skill's PETG range, so not overridden). Overrides meet print_requirements.json exactly as strength rounds 3/4 modelled the plate: 3 perimeters (1.26 mm band), 5 top / 5 bottom layers (1.0 mm skins), 25 % gyroid, 0.2 mm layers. Not raised: strength passes on these, the robot's mass budget counts every gram, and the slice already uses 7.76 of spec §7's 8 h. Elephant-foot 0.2 pairs with the 0.4 mm bed chamfer. Copies 1 = spec §7 (quantity 1, 8 h). Orientation is in the STL (brief): flat, underside on the bed, the four Ø10 columns standing. No library rows (materials.csv and lessons.md are empty), so no flow, temperature or xy compensation overrides. Seam: aligned (stated explicitly), the only mode that keeps seams off the coxa windows' 0.1 mm end-clearance faces: rear puts each seam at the loop's rearmost point, which on the LM and RM windows is a whole end face, and random scatters them over every face. Checked in the G-code: the window seams sit in corners, at the outboard end for LF, LM, RF and RM (the drop's governing corner, SF 3.39 with Kt 2.5) and at the inboard end for LR and RR; the columns' on their faces towards the body centre; the outline's on its +x edge at y 41.5. Because the outboard corners carry the strip's bending along the loop, staggered_inner_seams 1: the two inner perimeters now start 0.6 mm or more from the external seam instead of lining up with it at the corner. That only moves where each inner loop starts: layers, Z and extrusion are unchanged (it is not a staggered-layer trick), and time went 7.75 -> 7.76 h. The spec §8 drop test proves the corners as printed. Brim: none (brim_width 0): 19,700 mm² of PETG bed contact barely warps, and a brim would fill the 0.4 mm bed chamfer.
